findings.title: Cleanup uses r.log.Error for routine per-batch logging of full ID lists
findings.body: In CleanAnnotations, CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags and the batch callbacks, every batch logs 'Annotations to clean by time/count', 'Tags to clean' and 'cleaned ...' via r.log.Error, including the entire slice of IDs. These are normal operational/debug messages, not errors (the err field is often even nil at that point). Since the cleanup service now runs every minute, this will flood Grafana logs with error-level entries on every instance, including potentially thousands of IDs per line, polluting error dashboards and alerting. These should be Debug/Info level and should not log the full ID slices.

findings.title: Placeholder-based DELETE ... IN breaks on SQL Server when batch size exceeds ~2100 parameters
findings.body: deleteByIDs builds a DELETE with one '?' placeholder per ID and only special-cases SQLite's 999-parameter limit. SQL Server (a supported Grafana database) has a limit of 2100 parameters per statement. With AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize configured above 2100 (the PR's own test uses 32767), every batch DELETE will fail on SQL Server with a parameter-count error, breaking annotation cleanup entirely on that backend. The previous single-statement LIMIT-based approach had no such limit. The inlining fallback should also apply to (or otherwise handle) SQL Server, or the batch should be chunked to the dialect's parameter limit.

findings.title: Cleanup ticker reduced from 10 minutes to 1 minute without mention in PR description
findings.body: The Run loop ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, a 10x increase in frequency of all cleanup jobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, query history, annotations, etc.), but the PR description only discusses the deadlock fix. This behavior change is undocumented, increases background DB load, and combined with the new per-batch Error-level logging will multiply log volume tenfold. It should either be justified/reverted or documented, and the reviewer checklist ('notable improvement' docs) addressed.

findings.title: Log statements include a stale/always-nil err field
findings.body: The 'Annotations to clean by time'/'by count' and 'Tags to clean' log calls include an "err" key that is always nil at that point (the error case returns earlier), and the 'cleaned ...' calls log the error after already returning it upstream. This is misleading in log output and will confuse anyone investigating issues from logs; the err fields should be removed or the error handling restructured so errors are logged once, at the appropriate level.
